full_judgment:
Respondent No. 2, Eastern Bank Limited (hereinafter stated as the Bank) sanctioned and disbursed some loan in favour of Respondent No. 3, Gonophone Bangladesh Limited (shortly, Gonophone) and at the time of obtaining loan charge documents for the loan were signed by the directors of Gonophone and the directors also executed personal guarantee of the loan of Gonophone. The petitioner, Manik K. Bhattacharjee having resigned earlier as a director of Gonophone, he did not execute any charge documents, letter of guarantee, etc for the said loan. After resignation of the petitioner of the Board of Directors of Gonophone in a meeting dated 26-12-2002, accepted his resignation. Thereafter, the petitioner had transferred all his shares with the approval of the Board of Directors. However, the Bank sent the name of the petitioner as a director of Gonophone, a loan defaulter, to Bangladesh Bank and it was included in the CIB report of Bangladesh Bank. Therefore, the petitioner filed Writ Petition No. 8921 of 2005 in which a Rule was issued with an order of stay of the operation of the CIB report. The Managing Director of Gonophone filed Company Matter No. 174 of 2006 before the High Court Division for winding up of Gonophone under section 241 read with sections 242 and 245 of the Companies Act, 1994 (hereinafter stated as the Act) which was admitted by order dated 11-12-2006 and notice was published in the National Daily Newspaper as well as the Bangladesh Gazette fixing the date on 21-2-2007 for hearing. Meanwhile, the Bank filed Artha Rin Suit No. 219 of 2006 on 22-10-2006 before the Artha Rin Adalat No. 3, Dhaka (the Adalat) imp leading, the petitioner, Gonophone and others as defendants of the suit claiming the petitioner as a director of Gonophone. The Managing Director of Gonophone appeared in the suit prayed for time for filing written statement. Thereafter, Gonophone submitted an application under section 250 of the. Act praying for stay of further proceeding of Artha Rin Suit on the ground of filing of Company Matter No. 174 of 2005. The learned Judge of the Adalat adjourned hearing of the suit several times. The Company Matter was heard on 4-6-2007 and order was passed for winding up of Gonophone but, Gonophone was unable to file certified copy of the said judgment before the Adalat as the certified copy was not ready. The Adalat ultimately rejected the prayer of Gonophone and fixed a date for ex-parte hearing of the suit on 15-8-2007. On prayer of Gonophone exparte hearing was adjourned on 18-9-2007, 18-9-2007, 1-1-2007 and 23-10-2007 and ultimately on 23-10-2007 the learned Judge of the Adalat took up Artha Rin Suit No. 219 of 2006 for hearing and decreed exparte. The judgment-debtors having failed to pay the decretal amount, the Bank filed Artha Jari Case No. 34 of 2008 before the Adalat on 9-1-2008. Eventually, on prayer of the decree-holder Bank under section 34(I) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 (hereinafter called as the Ain), the learned Judge of the Adalat passed the impugned order dated 11-5-2008 issuing warrant against the judgment-debtors as no property was mortgaged in favour of the Bank and, as such, auction sale was not possible. This resulted in the writ petition. 

 3. The petitioner on 27-4-2005 filed a supplementary affidavit annexing certified copy of the application filed by the Bank under section 34(1) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 for issuance of warrant of arrest against the judgment-debtors and contending that Md Harunur Rashid, Senior Officer of the Bank had no lawful authority to file the application on behalf of the decree-holder Bank and therefore, the application is unlawful. 

 (3) Under section 26 of the Ain the provision of the Code was applicable in the execution case as no procedure has been enacted by the Parliament for civil prison/ warrant of arrest in execution of a decree passed by the Artha Rin Adalat. 

 14. The first question is whether the petitioner was a director of the Bank and he executed charge documents for the loan. It transpired from the writ petition that the Bank on 10-12-2001 sanctioned some loan to Respondent No. 3 Gonophone and disbursed it to Gonophone and that the directors of the Bank executed charge documents, letter of guarantee, etc, for the said loan. The petitioner in paragraph 6 of the writ petition stated that his resignation was accepted by the Board of director of 26-12-2002 which is after the loan sanction letter and this shares were transferred later on. Therefore, the disputed question of facts as to whether this petitioner executed any grantee for the loan or was director of Gonophone at the relevant time or whether his resignation was accepted by the Bank are all disputed question of facts which cannot be decided in writ jurisdiction without taking evidence Moreover, the suit was decreed in favour of the Bank and against the defendants including the petitioners. These questions cannot be raised in writ jurisdiction without challenging the judgment and decree in appropriate forum. Therefore, no decision is given on this question in this writ petition. 

 "51. Subject to such conditions and limitations as may be prescribed, the Court may, on the application of the decree-holder, order execution of the decree— 

 20. Provided that, where the decree is for the payment of money, execution by detention in prison shall not be ordered unless, after giving the judgment-debtor an opportunity of showing cause why he should not be committed to prison, the Court, for reasons recorded in writing, is satisfied— 

 (a) that the judgment-debtor, with the object or effect of obstructing of delaying the execution of the decree— 

 (ii) has, after the institution of the suit in which the decree was passed, dishonestly transferred, concealed, or removed any part of his property, or committed any other act of bad faith in relation to his property; or 

 (b) that the judgment-debtor has, or has since he date of the decree, the means to pay the amount of the decree or some substantial part thereof and refuses or neglects or has refused or neglected to pay the same, or 

 (c) that the decree is for a sum for which the judgment-debtor was bound in a fiduciary capacity to account. 

 Order XXI, rule 37 of the Code, Execution of Decrees and Orders 

 (1) Notwithstanding anything in these rules, where an application is for the execution of a decree for the payment of money by the arrest and detention in the civil prison of a judgment debtor who is liable to be arrested in pursuance of the application. The Court shall, instead of issuing a warrant for his arrest, issue a notice calling upon him to appear before the Court on a day to be specified in the notice and show cause why he should not be committed to the civil prison: 

 Provided that such notice shall not be necessary if the Court is satisfied, by affidavit, or otherwise, that, with the object or effect of delaying the execution of the decree, the judgment-debtor is likely to abscond or leave the local limits of the jurisdiction of the Court. 

 (2) Where appearance is not made in obedience to the notice, the Court shall, if the decree-holder so requires, issue a warrant for the arrest of the judgment for. 

 22. However, this provision is not also mandatory in all case as Order XXI, rule 37 also provides that such notice shall not be necessary if the Court is satisfied by affidavit of otherwise that with the object of delaying the execution of the decree, the judgment-debtor is likely abscond, etc. These provisions of section 51 and Order XXI, rule 37 of the Code are incorporated as a measure of punishment under certain circumstances. On the other hand, section 34 of the Ain empowers the Adalat to detain the judgment-debtor in civil prison (civil custody) as a measure of compel him to pay the decretal money and not as measure of punishment. 

 23. Therefore, object of section 51 read with Order XXI, rule 37 of the Code and the object of দেওয়ানী আটকাদেশ under section 34 are not the same. Moreover, the provisions of section 51 and Order XXI, rule 37 are relating to Money Decree passed in a Money Suit but not in a suit for recovery of loan by financial institution though it may be called a Money Decree but for the later a special law, the Ain, has been enacted by the Parliament. Section 34(10) of the Ain provides that if for any reason auction sale is not possible the judgment-debtor may be arrested and detained in civil prison/civil custody "সরাসরি" (directly) Since the word "সরাসরি" (directly) has been used in section 34 (10) of the Ain, it cannot be interpreted that prior show cause notice is necessary as the meaning of section 34(10) would be nugatory is such a case. Thus, the provisions of section 51 and Order XXI, rule 37 of the Code are in conflict with the provisions of section 34(1)(9)(10) of the Ain, Under section 26 of the Ain the provision of the Code is applicable so far as it is not inconsistent with the provisions of the Ain which includes the provisions of section 34 of the Ain, Moreover, under section 30 of the Ain special provision has been made for publishing notice after filing of the execution case under certain circumstances. 

 28. The cases reported in 22 BLD 153, 24 BLD 493 and 12 BLC (AD) 153 are all related to Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 1990 and there was no specific provision in the said Ain, 1990 for issuance of warrant of arrest/civil prison and the provisions of the Code were applicable in an execution case under Ain, 1990 relating to issuance of warrant of arrest. But specific provisions have been made in Chapter VII-Execution (৬ষ্ঠ পরিচচ্ছদ-জারী) of the Ain for execution of decree of Artha Rin suit,(দেওয়ানী আটকাদেশ) etc. Therefore, the said decisions have no manner of application in the instant case. 

 "the said provision of the Code of Civil Procedure speaks about issuance of show cause notice upon the judgment-debtor before issuing warrant of arrest as to why he should not be committed it civil prison without reference to any period of sentence for recovery of money pending execution proceeding, as a mode of punishment, whereas section 34 of the Ain, 2003 provides for civil detention to be passed against the judgment-debtor as a mode for realization of the decretal amount where the legislature has used the following language" As such, it cannot be said that Order XXI, rule 37 of the Code is identical with the provision laid down in section 34 of the Ain. Moreover, the notice as required under Order XXI, rule 37 of the Code is also not indispensable, rather it was followed by a proviso where the Court preserved the power not to issue such notice if it comes within the knowledge that in order to cause delay the judgment-debtor has been adopting dilatory tactics. More so, the said provision stands for money decree passed in a Money Suit but not in a suit for recovery of bank loan which may also be called an money decree for which special law exists for the said purpose e.g. Act VII of 2003. Accordingly, we are of the view that the said provision of the Code as to issuance of show cause notice cannot be allowed to be implemented alone leaving the proviso laid down therein in order to issue a warrant of arrest against the judgment -debtor under section 34(1) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003. Moreover, the judgment debtor has also enjoyed the privileges of such notice under section 30 of the Ain, 2003 which is not required in a Money Suit which is being governed by the Code of Civil Procedure. More so, since Order XXI, rule 37 of the Ain, hence, the application of the said provision is ousted in view of sections 3 and 26 of the Ain. 

 "We hold that the provision of the Code was only applicable so far as it is not inconsistent with the provisions of the Ain. Specific provisions for execution of decree laying been prescribed in the Ain which does not require issuance of show cause notice to the judgment-debtor before passing in order of civil imprisonment or warrant of arrest no show came notice to the judgment-debtor under of the Code was necessary."
